fixer.title: menus: Optimize one-shot menu action resolution

introducer.title: Don't listen on menu changed, method 2

cases.mechanism: Every one-shot menu lookup built and tore down event-tracking persistent-menu infrastructure, repeating registry scans, sorting, context-key collection, listener allocation, and disposal on synchronous per-row/per-selection paths.
cases.symptom: Synchronous menu resolution latency and allocation/GC pressure scaled with the number of selected or rendered tree elements and registered menu contributions.
cases.fixedBehavior: One-shot requests now call createMenuActionGroups directly, avoiding persistent-menu listeners, schedulers, dependency collection, and immediate disposal; filtering also occurs before sorting, bounding sort/action construction to contributions matching the current row context.
cases.evidence: The base getMenuActions implementation constructed MenuImpl, called getActions, and immediately disposed it. MenuImpl synchronously constructs MenuInfo, a RunOnceScheduler, a registry listener, disposable stores, and a debounce emitter; MenuInfo scans/sorts registry entries and collects context-key dependencies. Tree-view action resolution calls getMenuActions once for every selected element with a row-specific context, so all of that setup repeated serially per element even though no event could be observed before disposal. The added direct call at line 40 reads/filter/sorts the registry and constructs only the returned actions.
